The cold metal of the table bit into his bare skin. A throbbing pain pulsed in his neck, a dull counterpoint to the sterile hum that filled the room. Panic clawed at his throat, but the purple straps held him immobile, a prisoner in his own body. The last thing he remembered was the warm comfort of his bed. Now, harsh, unforgiving light assaulted his eyes, and the air tasted of antiseptic and something… alien.

Two figures loomed over him, their green-cyan skin shimmering in the harsh light. They were female, undeniably, their curves accentuated by the minimal attire they wore – only gloves, as far as he could see. Horns, purple and wickedly sharp, protruded from their heads, framing faces both beautiful and terrifying. Their yellow eyes, cold and calculating, scanned him with clinical detachment.

One of them, the one closer to his head, held a device that beeped softly. Her plump lips, painted a disturbing shade of green, remained fixed in a neutral expression. "Subject is stable, Xylara," she said, her voice a melodic drone that did little to soothe his rising fear. "Vital signs within acceptable parameters."

Xylara. The other one, the one whose gaze felt like a physical violation, stepped closer. Her eyes lingered on his body, assessing, evaluating. He tried to tug against the restraints, but they held fast, cold and unyielding against his wrists and ankles.

He was a prisoner, a tool, reduced to nothing more than a biological resource.
